```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  fig.width = 8,
  fig.height = 4,
  fig.align = "center",
  fig.retina = 2,
  out.width = "100%",
  cache.extra = packageVersion("interactmeta")
)
```

This article follows [`vignette("cams")`](cams.html). CAMS treats combined-effect
heterogeneity $\tau$ and interaction heterogeneity $\tau_\gamma$ as separate
blocks. `heterogeneity()` tabulates them; `plot(fit, type = "heterogeneity")`
draws Bayesian marginals or frequentist profile views. `traceplot()` applies only
to Bayesian fits (`bayesmeta` shrinkage-vs-$\tau$ panels for the interaction and
combined blocks).

```{r setup, cache = TRUE}
library(interactmeta)

des_age <- ifrac(age, reference = "Younger")
fit_age <- cams(
  des_age,
  reference = "Younger",
  tau.prior = function(tau) bayesmeta::dhalfnormal(tau, scale = 0.5),
  tau.interaction.prior = function(tau_gamma)
    bayesmeta::dhalfnormal(tau_gamma, scale = 0.1)
)
```

Half-normal `tau.prior` and `tau.interaction.prior` follow the immunotherapy
example in [`vignette("cams")`](cams.html); use `method = "REML"` on the same
[ifrac()] output when you only need frequentist heterogeneity panels.

## Bayesian heterogeneity and traceplots (`age`)

```{r het-table}
heterogeneity(fit_age)
summary(fit_age)$heterogeneity$summary
```

[heterogeneity()] defaults to `component = "all"` with `summary = TRUE`.
Request `component = "intercept"` or `"slope"` for one CAMS block, set `prob`
for interval coverage, or `summary = FALSE` to keep posterior `draws` only.
[summary()] exposes the same rows in `$heterogeneity$summary`.

```{r het-plot, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
plot(fit_age, type = "heterogeneity")
```

`plot(fit, type = "heterogeneity")` calls [plot_heterogeneity()] with `which =
"both"` (τ and τ_γ side by side). On REML fits with τ̂ at the boundary, panels
show **metafor** profiles rather than sharp posteriors. Use `which =
"interaction"` or `"combined"` for a single panel; `prior = TRUE` overlays the
stored τ prior on Bayesian plots. See [`?plot_heterogeneity`] for ggplot
fallbacks (`probs`, `bins`, `colours`, `base_size`).

## Traceplots (`age`)

```{r trace-int, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
traceplot(fit_age, type = "interaction")
```

```{r trace-comb, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
traceplot(fit_age, type = "combined")
```

[`?traceplot`] documents `ylab`, `xlab`, and **bayesmeta** passthrough (`mulim`,
`taulim`, `ci`, `prior`, colours). `type = "modifiers"` is intentionally
unsupported: orthogonal CAMS stores interaction and combined native objects
only. [traceplot()] requires `method = "Bayesian"` on [cams()].

## Frequentist heterogeneity plot (`steroids`)

The REACT `steroids` REML fit from [`vignette("cams")`](cams.html) often
estimates $\tau$ and $\tau_\gamma$ at zero; the heterogeneity panel then
reflects the fitted metafor random-effects structure rather than an
informative profile.

```{r reml-setup, cache = TRUE}
library(metafor)

steroids_es <- escalc(
  measure = "OR",
  ai = treat.events, bi = treat.total - treat.events,
  ci = cont.events, di = cont.total - cont.events,
  data = steroids
)
des_st <- ifrac(steroids_es, reference = "Non-IMV")
fit_reml <- cams(des_st, reference = "Non-IMV", method = "REML")
```

```{r het-reml-table}
heterogeneity(fit_reml)
```

```{r het-reml-plot, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
plot(fit_reml, type = "heterogeneity")
```

The REML table uses the same [heterogeneity()] API as the Bayesian `age` fit;
`plot(fit_reml, type = "heterogeneity", ...)` forwards `prob` and `which` to
[plot_heterogeneity()]. Profile shading and cutoff labels follow the fitted
**metafor** `rma` blocks when τ is estimated at zero.
